context: A uni student interviews a retired biography author at home
purpose: Teach: 情緒/カリスマ/一族/推理/調停/活字/イデオロギー/頭脳

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: 本日はお時間を頂きありがとうございます。先生は推理小説の評伝で知られていますが、最初に手がけたのはどの作家でしたか？
lines.en: Thank you for your time today. You're known for biographies of mystery writers — which author did you tackle first?
lines.style: Polite interview opening, slightly nervous student tone, formal register.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ある旧家の一族に生まれた作家でね。彼の頭脳明晰な文章に、若い私はすっかり魅了されたんだ。
lines.en: He was born into an old family clan. His brilliantly sharp prose completely captivated me when I was young.
lines.style: Warm reminiscing elder voice, slow nostalgic delivery, gentle smile audible.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: その方は文壇でもカリスマ的な存在だったと伺いました。直接お会いになって、印象はいかがでしたか？
lines.en: I've heard he was a charismatic figure in literary circles. What was your impression when you met him?
lines.style: Curious follow-up question, leaning forward, respectful student curiosity.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: それがね、お会いすると意外と物静かで、情緒の細やかな方だった。活字の上の鋭さとは別人のようでね。
lines.en: Well, in person he was surprisingly quiet, with a delicate emotional sensitivity — quite different from the sharpness on the page.
lines.style: Thoughtful elder reflecting, soft chuckle, savoring an old memory.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: 評伝を書く中で、ご家族との関係について書くのは難しくなかったですか？特に遺族との調停のような場面もあったのでは。
lines.en: Was writing about his family relationships difficult? I imagine there were moments almost like mediation with surviving relatives.
lines.style: Probing but respectful, lowering voice slightly for sensitive topic.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: 鋭いところを突くね。実際、戦後のイデオロギー対立がご家族の中にも影を落としていてね、何度も話し合いを重ねたよ。
lines.en: You strike a sharp point. The postwar ideological conflicts had cast shadows within the family too, so we had many discussions.
lines.style: Impressed at the question, grave tone shift, weighted with history.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: なるほど…。最後に、これから評伝を書きたい若い書き手に向けて、一言頂けますか？
lines.en: I see... Lastly, could you give a word of advice to young writers hoping to write biographies?
lines.style: Quiet awe, transitioning to closing question, notebook closing tone.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: 対象を神格化せず、対等な人間として見ることだ。それが伝記作家にとって、何より大切な姿勢だと私は思うよ。
lines.en: Don't deify your subject — see them as an equal human being. That, I believe, is the most important stance for a biographer.
lines.style: Concluding wisdom, firm but kind, like passing a torch.
